source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 224: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 224: do not select tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) from the prompt alone; collect platform measurements first. Assume the model graph, layer shapes, precision, parameter and activation memory, GPU count/type and usable HBM (GiB), topology and link bandwidth, software versions, clocks, request lengths, arrival rate, concurrency, batching, and latency/throughput/error/quality/availability SLO thresholds are specified; label estimates. Enumerate feasible TP degrees and balanced PP partitions, rejecting any option without positive memory headroom. Hypothesis: for a fixed representative workload on identical hardware, the feasible design with lower held-out p99 end-to-end latency while meeting every SLO gate is better; falsify it when p99 is not lower or any gate fails. Warm up, randomize paired trials, tune on a disjoint set, and evaluate on held-out requests with workload mix, arrival rate, precision, clocks, concurrency, and batch policy held constant. Measure compute, TP collective or PP activation-transfer time, synchronization wait, stage imbalance, pipeline bubbles, queueing, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, quality, availability, memory headroom, and recovery time, with units and uncertainty. TP may reduce per-GPU memory but adds frequent topology-sensitive collectives; PP may reduce collectives but requires balanced stages and enough microbatches and adds bubbles, transfers, and queueing. Control thermal/software drift, background load, stragglers, and request mix. Test failure/reconfiguration only if authorized, isolated, bounded, redacted, and reversible. Canary the winner and roll back on tail-latency, error, quality, availability, memory, or recovery-budget regression. This is provisional calibration and requires domain-expert review.
risks: Missing platform facts and SLO thresholds prevent a universal winner.
Tail latency is sensitive to batching, queueing, stage imbalance, collectives, stragglers, and drift.
Failure testing can disrupt service without authorization and isolation.
evidence_required: Per-GPU memory/headroom and feasible topology-aware TP/PP configurations.
Repeated randomized paired trials with disjoint tuning and held-out p50/p95/p99, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, error, quality, and availability results.
Authorized recovery/rollback rehearsal and domain-expert review.
